records.student_text: A hanging sign remains at rest while its support forces balance its weight. What kind of equilibrium is this?
records.student_html:
A hanging sign remains at rest while its support forces balance its weight. What kind of equilibrium is this?

  1. static equilibrium
  2. dynamic equilibrium
  3. unbalanced motion
  4. no-force state
records.solution_text: static equilibrium matches the motion state while the net force is zero.
records.solution_html: static equilibrium matches the motion state while the net force is zero.

records.student_text: The book is resting on the table. Use the weight and support arrows to explain why rest does not mean that no forces are acting.
records.student_html:
The book is resting on the table. Use the weight and support arrows to explain why rest does not mean that no forces are acting.

  1. The opposing forces can balance so their vector sum is zero even though individual forces are present.
  2. An object at rest cannot have any forces acting.
  3. Inertia creates an upward force that removes all other forces.
  4. Only gravitational force matters when speed is zero.

choices.text: The opposing forces can balance so their vector sum is zero even though individual forces are present.
An object at rest cannot have any forces acting.
Inertia creates an upward force that removes all other forces.
Only gravitational force matters when speed is zero.

records.student_text: A suspended light is in vertical equilibrium. One cable pulls upward with 19 N and a second cable pulls upward with 29 N while the light’s weight is 48 N downward. Use \(\Sigma F_y\) to determine the net force.
records.student_html:
A suspended light is in vertical equilibrium. One cable pulls upward with 19 N and a second cable pulls upward with 29 N while the light’s weight is 48 N downward. Use \(\Sigma F_y\) to determine the net force.

  1. 0 N
  2. 67 N
  3. 29 N
  4. cannot be determined because the object is moving

choices.text: cannot be determined because the object is moving

records.solution_text: Upward total is 19+29=48 N, equal to the 48 N downward weight, so ΣF_y=0.
records.solution_html: Upward total is 19+29=48 N, equal to the 48 N downward weight, so ΣF_y=0.
